tools.name: get_tool_pick_rate
tools.description: For a developer tool (product name or npm package, e.g. 'Clerk', 'next-auth', '@supabase/supabase-js'), returns how often 6 AI models recommend it first, mention it, and actually use it in apps they build, with its rank and main competitor. Covers auth, databases and email.

tools.name: get_category_ranking
tools.description: Ranks the tools AI models recommend first and the tools they actually install in AI-built apps, for one category: auth, database or email.

tools.name: check_package_freshness
tools.description: Checks dependencies (an object of package name to version range, as in package.json) against the npm registry. Returns packages that are a major version or more behind npm's latest, deprecated packages, and the current major to use. Useful before installing packages from memory.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_tool_pick_rate, get_category_ranking · Private data: get_category_ranking · Public sink: get_tool_pick_rate, get_category_ranking.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_tool_pick_rate, get_category_ranking · Private data: get_category_ranking · Public sink: get_tool_pick_rate, get_category_ranking

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
